newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MOELLER STRIKES TWICE AS DORTMUND RETURN WITH 3-1 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOELLER STRIKES TWICE AS DORTMUND RETURN WITH 3-1 WIN.

text.p: German international Andy Moeller struck twice as champions Borussia Dortmund began the second half of the Bundesliga season with an impressive 3-1 home victory over Bayer Leverkusen to go top of the table on Friday.
In the first day of action since the league's two-month winter break, Dortmund came from behind to take a one-point lead over Bayern Munich who play hosts to St. Pauli on Saturday.

Third-placed Leverkusen took the early initiative in front of a capacity 55,000 crowd when Brazilian Paulo Sergio scored in the seventh minute after a defensive blunder. The Brazilian was unchallenged as he fired home from close range.
But 10 minutes later midfielder Moeller headed a superb cross from the left from Knut Reinhardt into the left-hand corner to equalise.
Seconds after the break Swiss striker Stephane Chapuisat put the champions in front after Germany's Euro 96 libero Matthias Sammer set him free in the penalty area with a clever pass.
Moeller sealed the issue in the 89th minute with a spectacular second goal, a powerful shot into the top left-hand corner from about 16 metres.
"That was a top-class match. We had to go to our limits," Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said. "I'm delighted with our performance."

In the night's other match Cologne beat struggling Fortuna Duesseldorf 2-0. Austrian Toni Polster gave them the lead in the 45th minute and Fortuna defender Joerg Bach put through his own net six minutes from time.
